subject.title: [Security] Session hijacking vulnerability due to predictable sequence IDs in gateway client

question: Should the gateway security owner close this report as an unsupported threat model, or request a concrete trace showing that guessed `seq` values cross the authenticated RPC boundary?
rationale: Protected security labels require an explicit owner decision, while current source and protocol contracts do not support the claimed attack mechanism or the proposed cryptographic changes.

options.title: Close after boundary confirmation
options.body: Confirm that `seq` has no security authority and close the report unless a reproducible authentication or authorization bypass is supplied.

options.title: Request a concrete proof
options.body: Keep the report pending briefly for a WebSocket trace or proof of concept showing an unauthenticated or under-scoped connection injecting an accepted request.

recommendation.title: Close after boundary confirmation
recommendation.body: Confirm that `seq` has no security authority and close the report unless a reproducible authentication or authorization bypass is supplied.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged changes directly hardened WebSocket authentication scopes and the affected authorization boundary.
